failover_query.question: What is the payment rail failover procedure?
failover_query.answer_text:
**10:15 Jordan Lim:** From the September drill notes: the failover procedure worked, but flipping
  `rail_router` to RAIL_B_ONLY took about 4 minutes to reach all payment workers, not 2. [E1] Rail-A reliability was the main operational risk: two SEV-2 incidents in Q3, both handled with
  the failover procedure; no customer funds were lost. [E2] No customer funds are missing: every payment settled on Rail-A. [E4] **09:00 John Tan:** Heads-up for everyone: we are moving part of our outbound payment traffic to
  a second payment rail, **Rail-B**, operated by Vegaline Settlement. [E5] | Vendor                 | Service                         | Contract ends | Support SLA                 |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------- | --------------------------- |
| Orionix Clearing       | Rail-A, primary payment rail    | 2027-06-30    | SEV-1 response in 15 min    |
| Vegaline Settlement    | Rail-B, secondary payment rail  | 2028-05-31    | SEV-1 response in 20 min    |
| Cobalt Identity Checks | KYC document verification       | 2027-01-31    | 99.5% monthly availability  |
| Larkspur Cloud Hosting | Primary cloud region            | 2027-12-31    | 99.95% monthly availability |
| Tern Card Processing   | Card issuing and authorisations | 2027-09-30    | SEV-1 response in 30 min    | [E6] Per the failover procedure, the Rail-B prefunding account must hold
  SGD 2.5M before the weekend. [E1] Rail-A acknowledgements were slow again overnight. p95 peaked at
  70 seconds, so still under the 90-second failover trigger, but trending up for three nights. [E1]
